title: The section-normalized completed-linear restriction/pullback comparison
statement: Use the coefficient conventions [def-trf-coefficient-conventions] and point Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For a finite-field datum D, a prime l and a finite-dimensional coefficient extension E/Q_l, write c for coefficientSequenceRestriction on Spec D.k and G_r for ordinary sequence pullback at the r-th Frobenius power [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems, def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. Write H_r for the termwise completed-module inverse image [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison, def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations]. There is a unique natural isomorphism j_r:c⋙H_r≅G_r⋙c such that, for every system M, level n, site object U and section x over the reindexed object Phi_r(U), its component sends the scalar-restriction cast of x to the scalar-restriction cast of the tensor-unit sequence generator of x, restricted along the specified isomorphism comma arrow. These are the actual site arrows, coefficient actions, generator and casts of the recorded models, not independently chosen identifications. No constructibility, completeness or finite-output condition is assumed. This is the unchanged original declaration IntegralPointTransportTower.restrictionComparison_existsUnique, now placed in a separate compilation unit.

source.place: Agent-formulated prerequisite to clause (3): point transport on arbitrary simultaneous output systems and its whole-limit normalization; the blueprint asserts the application, not this stronger comparison lemma. Original j_r subclaim, preserved without strengthening or weakening.

proof.text: Apply WeilConjectures.integralTowerInverseImageUnit_existsUnique to the scheme isomorphism ((pointFrobeniusAut D)^r).hom. Its arbitrary-scheme source and target are both Spec D.k. The definitions ordinaryInverseTower and ordinaryPullback are exactly the tower inverse image and sequence pullback used there, so the isomorphism type, every tensor-unit section formula, and uniqueness specialize without any casts or additional hypotheses.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03D6, 03CZ and 0941; C6 specializes the already proved integralTowerInverseImageUnit_existsUnique (def-trf-integral-tower-inverse-image-unit) to Frobenius powers. The arbitrary-isomorphism proof constructs the actual adjunction unit and comma restriction, retains all quotient transitions, and proves uniqueness sectionwise.

theorem restrictionComparison_existsUnique (r : ℕ) :
    ∃! j : coefficientSequenceRestriction l E (Spec (.of D.k)) ⋙ ordinaryInverseTower D l E r ≅
        ordinaryPullback D l E r ⋙ coefficientSequenceRestriction l E (Spec (.of D.k)),
      ∀ (M : coefficientSequenceModules l E (Spec (.of D.k))) (n : ℕ) (U : (Spec (.of D.k)).ProEt)
        (x : M.val.obj (op (n, (proEtaleIsoPostcompose
          ((pointFrobeniusAut D) ^ r).hom).obj U))),
        (((j.hom.app M).app (op n)).val.app (op U))
          (integralComparisonRestrictedSection l E (Spec (.of D.k)) M n
            (op ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose ((pointFrobeniusAut D) ^ r).hom).obj U)) x) =
        integralComparisonRestrictedSection l E (Spec (.of D.k))
          ((ordinaryPullback D l E r).obj M) n (op U)
          (((ordinaryPullback D l E r).obj M).val.map
            (CategoryTheory.Prod.mkHom (𝟙 n)
              (proEtaleIsoCommaArrow ((pointFrobeniusAut D) ^ r).hom U)).op
            (integralComparisonSequenceGenerator l E ((pointFrobeniusAut D) ^ r).hom M n
              ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose ((pointFrobeniusAut D) ^ r).hom).obj U) x))
